title: Introduce reference compactors and adaptive index tiling
creator: Ava Chen
description: This ticket addresses recurring control-plane query regressions caused by wide FK chains and noisy sparse lookup tables. The approach is twofold: 1) deploy a lightweight reference compactor service that consolidates rarely-changing reference rows into dense canonical references (reduce row-width and duplicated lookups); 2) introduce an adaptive index tiling strategy for hot lookup tables that creates short-lived, rolling partial indexes (tiles) tuned to recent query shapes. Goal: reduce p95 read latency for tenant-scoped joins by 30% and cut index maintenance IO during bulk writes.
acceptance_criteria: p95 latency for tenant lookup queries reduced by >=30% on staging compared to baseline (see grafana dashboard)
end-to-end smoke test for control-plane list/create/update flows passes with no functional regressions
reference compactor runs as a controller with metrics and backpressure controls
adaptive index tiling has a configurable retention window and can be toggled per-table without downtime
migration scripts apply online with <5s write pause and a documented rollback path
implementation_notes: Reference compactor is a small worker that deduplicates canonical lookup records into a compact table ref.compacted_references (schema: ref_id, canonical_id, version, last_seen)
Workers will emit events to changefeed which the serving layer subscribes to for updating in-memory lookup caches
Adaptive tiling will create partial indexes named idx_<table>_tile_<epoch> and a controller keeps N active tiles per table based on recency windows
Index creations use CONCURRENTLY where supported; for Postgres-like clusters ensure maintenance_work_mem and statement_timeout alignment
Add telemetry: tile creation time, index size, index hit ratio, compactor run duration, and rollback events
progress_updates: 2026-02-16: Spike complete. Benchmarked compaction approach on a 10M-row tenant dataset; observed 28% reduction in join return rows when compaction applied locally.
2026-02-22: Design review with DB infra and runtime teams. Decided to keep compactor idempotent and append-only for initial rollout to avoid synchronous deletes.
2026-03-02: Proof-of-concept PR opened for reference compactor service (see PR list). Initial schema DDL drafted and reviewed by @sophia-ops.
2026-03-09: Staging rollout started for adaptive tiling controller on low-traffic tenant subset (tenant ids 1000-1100). Observed decreased read amplification, monitoring in grafana.
2026-03-10: Discovered edge-case with multi-tenant lookup cache invalidation; added a short-term lockless tombstone marker to avoid stale references during tile rotation

https://github.com/redwood-inference/control-plane/pull/1302 - migration SQL and feature flag integration
migrations: 2026-03-07: V2026_03_07__tile_index_controller_metadata.sql - adds control table ref.index_tiles and index metadata
Notes: Backfill uses chunked queries via primary key ranges, throttled by compactor concurrency setting. Backfill runbook: https://confluence.redwood/infrastructure/compactor-backfill
rollback_plan: Feature-flagged rollout. If severe regressions are observed, flip feature-flag to disable compactor and tile-controller; run DROP INDEX CONCURRENTLY for recently-created tiles and rehydrate original indexes from snapshot. For compactor changes, re-queue backfill tasks to restore canonical references from historical audit table and perform a safe rename swap. Documented rollback runbook linked in links.
testing_plan: Unit tests for compactor idempotency and versioning
Integration tests: simulated multi-tenant load with mixed read/write, assert cache invalidation correctness
Staging performance test: 48h run with production-like query mix and synthetic skews to verify tiling heuristics
Chaos test: kill compactor worker mid-backfill to validate recovery and no-write anomalies
risk: Index churn: frequent tile creation could increase WAL and IO — mitigated by retention window and creation caps
Stale references: caching layer might serve stale canonical ids during tile rotation — mitigated by tombstone markers and quick invalidation hooks
Rollback complexity: backfilling to previous state could be time-consuming; we limit initial rollout to safe tenant subsets
Storage cost: temporary index storage spike during tile overlap windows — monitor and set alert thresholds
